To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the Latino Health for ALL Coalition's action plan to promote physical activity was successful, and 2) the intervention to promote physical inactivity among Latino youth was successful.

1) the informal, flyer-based promotion of weekly soccer sessions was effective in attracting overweight and Latino youth, 2) youth attended the weekly sessions on average 4.2 times, and 3) youth were able to accumulate 18.8 - 22.2 min of moderate-to-vigorously physical activity per session.

1) a flyer-based campaign was effective in attracting Latino youth to structured soccer sessions, 2) these sessions enabled youth to accumulate about 20 minutes of moderate-to- vigorous physical activity, and 3) a family-based intervention was effective in promoting physical activity in Latino children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
promoting physical activity among Latino children and youth.
the promotion of physical activity among Latino youth.
understanding how community coalitions and families work together to promote healthy lifestyles in Latino children and youth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two studies presented in this dissertation provide empirical evidence that both community and family interventions can be effective at promoting physical activity among Latino youth.
both the community and family intervention efforts were successful in promoting physical activity in Latino children and youth.
the two interventions described in this study were effective in promoting physical activity among Latino children and youth in Kansas City.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that it is possible to promote physical activity through community-based efforts, and that it is possible for families of Latino children to promote physical activity within their home settings.
our research has provided evidence that community coalitions can be effective in addressing and preventing physical inactivity in Latino youth.
we have developed a community coalition that is committed to addressing chronic diseases, particularly obesity, in Latino communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
community coalitions are an effective way of addressing health problems in a community and that they are an effective way to bring about change at multiple levels.

it's not enough just to provide physical activity opportunities to Latino youth; it's important that the physical activity opportunities are enjoyable, and that they are promoted in a manner that reaches a broad spectrum of youth.
it is possible to promote physical activity and healthy lifestyles among Latino youth in the United States, and that community coalitions play an essential role in these efforts.
